claims.text: db/queries/index-demo.sql creates a temporary table order_log from generate_series(1, 200000), one row per minute counted from timestamptz '2026-01-01 00:00:00+07', so exactly one of the 200,000 rows has placed_at = '2026-01-02 03:04:00+07'.

claims.text: A TEMPORARY table exists only for the session that created it (here, one run of psql) and is dropped when that session ends, so the script rebuilds it on every run.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SQL Commands: CREATE TABLE (TEMPORARY | TEMP)

claims.text: With no index it can use for the condition, PostgreSQL answers a WHERE by a sequential scan: it reads every row of the table and applies the condition to each. EXPLAIN prints this as 'Seq Scan on <table>' with the condition on a 'Filter' line.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §14.1 Using EXPLAIN (Seq Scan example, Filter line); ch. 11 Indexes §11.1

claims.text: An index is a structure stored separately from the table; the default (B-tree) index keeps the indexed values in sorted order, each entry carrying the location of the table row the value came from.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs ch. 11 Indexes §11.1-§11.2 (B-tree default, sorted order); §73.2 B-Tree Structure

claims.text: An index scan searches the index for the entries satisfying the condition and reads only the table rows those entries point to. EXPLAIN prints it as 'Index Scan using <index> on <table>' with the condition on an 'Index Cond' line.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §14.1 Using EXPLAIN (Index Scan, Index Cond); §11.1

claims.text: A condition on a Filter line is checked for each row the node scans, and only rows that pass are output; the same condition shown as Index Cond is used to search the index, so the rows it rejects are never read from the table.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §14.1 Using EXPLAIN (Filter versus Index Cond)

claims.text: An index occupies disk space and has to stay synchronised with its table, which adds overhead to data manipulation: every INSERT and every UPDATE that changes an indexed column writes index entries too, and rows removed by DELETE leave entries the database cleans up later.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs ch. 11 Indexes §11.1 (keeping an index synchronised adds overhead to data modification)

claims.text: EXPLAIN prints the plan the planner generates for the statement and does not execute that statement unless ANALYZE is given; COSTS OFF omits the estimated startup and total cost numbers from the output.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SQL Commands: EXPLAIN (Description; ANALYZE, COSTS options)

claims.text: CREATE INDEX <name> ON <table> (<column>) builds an index on that column; ANALYZE <table> collects statistics about the table's contents — among them how many rows it holds and how the values of a column spread — which the planner then uses when it chooses a plan.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SQL Commands: CREATE INDEX (Synopsis); ANALYZE (Description); §14.2 Statistics Used by the Planner

claims.text: An index on a column cannot serve a condition that applies a function to that column, such as date(placed_at) = '2026-01-02', because the index stores the column's values and not the function's results.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §11.7 Indexes on Expressions; §14.1 Using EXPLAIN

claims.text: A B-tree index can serve a LIKE pattern only when the pattern is a constant anchored to the start of the string, so a search such as LIKE '%webcam%' cannot use it.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §11.2 Index Types (B-tree with LIKE, pattern anchored to the beginning of the string)

claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, psql reference, Options: -e / --echo-queries

claims.text: PostgreSQL creates a unique index automatically for a PRIMARY KEY and for a UNIQUE constraint (a column declared to hold no repeated value); declaring a foreign key with REFERENCES creates no index on the referencing column, which is why indexing it is often suggested.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §5.4 Constraints (unique constraint creates a unique index; foreign keys: index the referencing columns); CREATE INDEX (Notes)

claims.text: In db/schema.sql at stage-0, orders.customer_id is declared 'integer NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id)' and no CREATE INDEX statement exists in the file, so no index covers that column.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/schema.sql lines 18-24 (and whole file: no CREATE INDEX)

claims.text: Adding EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF) SELECT * FROM order_log WHERE customer_id = 3 to the end of index-demo.sql gives a Seq Scan: order_log carries only the placed_at index, and the file's first line sets max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 0 for the session.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/queries/index-demo.sql lines 3, 16; PostgreSQL 17 docs §14.1; §15.2 When Can Parallel Query Be Used

claims.text: A column you filter or join on often is a candidate for an index when the reads it speeds up matter more than the writes it slows down; an index no query searches is cost without return.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 2 and 3

claims.text: db/queries/index-demo.sql sets max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 0 above the quoted excerpt, which disables parallel query execution for the session, so no plan the file prints can grow the extra lines a parallel plan adds: each one is two lines, the scan step and its condition.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/queries/index-demo.sql line 3; PostgreSQL 17 docs §20.4 max_parallel_workers_per_gather; §15.2 When Can Parallel Query Be Used

claims.text: ANALYZE only updates the statistics the planner reads; it opens no new way to reach a row, so the access path the second plan uses comes from CREATE INDEX and not from ANALYZE.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SQL Commands: ANALYZE (Description); ch. 11 Indexes §11.1; §14.2 Statistics Used by the Planner

One clause says the file switches off the helpers PostgreSQL can split one scan across — needed to account for the shape of the printed plans; the term 'parallel worker' is not used and the planner detail is not opened.
